summary.text: A 66-year-old man was referred to the hospital with a left ventricular mass detected incidentally during transthoracic echocardiography performed prior to a cholecystectomy. He had no cardiac symptoms or history of embolism, normal heart sounds without any cardiac murmurs, and normal chest radiography, electrocardiography and blood examinations.

Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a mobile mass, 16 mm in diameter, originating from the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle, and computed tomography showed a homogeneous 20-mm-diameter tumor with an extremely short stalk. The case presentation also reports a short stalk, direct attachment of the tumor to the ventricular wall, left ventricular diameters of 52 mm in the diastolic phase and 30 mm in the systolic phase, and an ejection fraction estimated as 80 %.

The transaortic and transmitral approaches were considered inadequate, and a transventricular approach was planned preoperatively and adopted. Under general anesthesia, the heart was exposed through a median thoracotomy and the tumor was observed via transesophageal echocardiography; the incision line was planned under echo-guidance and its final location was determined by epicardial echocardiography. Cardiopulmonary bypass was instituted and the heart was arrested with cardioplegia.

A 3-cm-long ventriculotomy was placed between the first diagonal and obtuse marginal branches. A gelatinous 18-mm mass was directly visualized and found to originate from the trabecular muscle, and the distance from the incision line to the edge of the stalk was 5 mm. The tumor was completely resected in an en bloc fashion with a margin over 5 mm, and the ventriculotomy was closed with mattress sutures, a running suture and Teflon felt strips.

Histopathological examination demonstrated typical features of myxoma, a good surgical margin over 5 mm and no evidence of invasion. The postoperative course was uneventful. Echocardiography showed left ventricular diastolic and systolic diameters of 50 and 26 mm and an ejection fraction of 85 % at discharge, and 51 and 30 mm and 75 % at 6 months after the surgery; no recurrence or arrhythmia was seen in the 24 months since the operation.
